question: Resolve the Dow/Rohm and Haas Bristol site through its original FRS and RCRA program records, then record the corporate acquisition and distinguish it from ownership of all historic study areas.
answer: The June 2020 decision says Dow purchased Rohm and Haas in 2009 and identifies it as a wholly owned subsidiary. The EPA profile describes a much broader historic chemical site, including North Parcel areas owned by Heritage Conservancy and Bristol Township. Register the corporate acquisition separately from parcel title and retained remedy duties; neither the registry address nor the acquisition proves that the target owns the entire historic footprint.

evidence.quote: 4. Description of Contamination & Remedy The former WWTP Area is the out-of-service portion of the former wastewater treatment plant at the Rohm and Haas Bristol Plant. The former WWTP Area occupies about 70 acres located west of Route 413, between River Road and the Delaware River, where untreated and treated water basins remain from the former WWTP. The area for Act 2 Closure consists of basins identified as Solid Waste Management Units (SWMUs) l, 2, 7, and 8 and the area of concern (AOC) identified as the Former Burning Area (See Exhibit B, Figure 2). Rohm and Haas submitted to the Department an Act 2 Final Report for soil and sediment in the former WWTP Area dated October 2012 and an Addendum to the Final Report dated March 2013. The Final Report and Addendum characterized soil and sediment quality in the former WWTP Area and demonstrated attainment of Act 2 standards as discussed below. The Department approved the Final Report and Addendum by letter dated March 25, 2013. Soil Quality Characterization of surface and subsurface soils in the former WWTP Area showed that soils met the residential statewide health standard because there were no exceedances of the Residential Direct Contact medium specific concentration (MSC) or the soil to groundwater MSC.
